stem: A former preterm infant is attending a neonatal follow-up clinic at 10 months corrected age, and the team wants a developmental assessment tool with separate expressive and receptive language scales; which tool is the best fit?

options.text: Bayley Scale of Infant and Toddler Development
Wechsler Preschool and Primary Scales of Intelligence

explanation: Bayley Scale of Infant and Toddler Development is the best fit for this infant. It is used from early infancy through toddlerhood, is commonly used in neonatal follow-up clinics, and includes separate expressive and receptive language scales.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Formalised Developmental Assessment

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because Griffiths III is a broader developmental assessment tool, but the age range and the separate expressive and receptive language scales point more specifically to Bayley.
optionExplanations.B: Correct because it is appropriate for infants and toddlers, is commonly used in neonatal follow-up clinics, and includes separate expressive and receptive language assessment.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because ADOS is an autism diagnostic observation tool, not the main developmental assessment used for this neonatal follow-up scenario.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because the Wechsler Preschool and Primary Scales of Intelligence is intended for older children, not a 10-month corrected age infant.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because Mary Sheridan 'From Birth to 5 Years' is a developmental surveillance reference rather than the formal developmental assessment tool described.
